Free State & Ace Magashule: Mxolisi Dukwana blows the whistle

By: Joy Summers | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
One liner tonight on Carte Blanche A province besieged by corruption, its former premier Ace Magashule implicated by his one- time friend and colleague Mxolisi Dukwana at the Zondo Commission. Will

Unique Selling Point:
Unique Selling point
Candid Interview with whistleblower Mxolisi Dukwana who has taken on ACE Magashule who some describe as South Africa’s most dangerous politician 400 pages of candid testimony already in the Zondo commission but fractured, technical and not well covered as it was over shadowed by the death of Gavin Watson.


Summary:
Summary
Hardly a week goes by in our politics when another salvo is fired in the ongoing battle between President Cyril Ramaphosa and Secretary General Ace Magashule. Cartoonists show the president being stabbed in the back by Magashule, or having concrete poured over his boots by a smiling Secretary General. But this battle is a battle for the soul of the ANC and by implication for the country.

The president seen as offering the possibility of a stable country, Magashule seen to represent the fight back campaign that will take the country down the path of Venezuela.

For nearly a decade Ace Magashule has had the run of the Free State. Allegations of corruption, lies and deceit are only part of his story. His name provokes fear and although there are allegations and even a book about his exploits, nothing ever sticks to Ace Magashule. Now his one- time friend and colleague from the ANC PEC and the Free State Government, Mxolisi Dukwana, has blown the whistle under oath at the Zondo Commission. Will his testimony carry weight, will Magashule and his patronage system be held to account and can it alter the landscape of our politics?

Carte Blanche goes behind the story told at the Zondo commission and finds out why with this whistleblower from Welkom put it all on the line.



Further information:
FURTHER INFORMATION
The Zondo commission had a tough time keeping Mxolisi Dukwana to his statement. He is like an encyclopedia of Free State corruption, and now that he has chosen to take on the former premier, a former minister and named 30 public and private beneficiaries of corruption in his testimony, he is contacted all the time by others with their own stories of corruption, those who are too fearful to come to the commission.

His latest testimony in August runs to nearly 400 pages. He implicates officials, policemen, business men, pastors and even the Free State Judiciary, whom he says have wives who do business with the provincial government. Another high- ranking official known only as Mr X , but known to Carte Blanche, is also implicated in helping to provide political cover at National level for what Dukwana calls the Asbestos Heist – A R255 million-rand audit of Asbestos rooftops that wasn’t needed.

“If our law enforcement agencies were well oiled Mr Magashule and all those who aided ad abetted this asbestos audit should be doing time in jail.

He went on:

“To date no eradication of asbestos roofs has been carried out in any township in the Free State…I invite the commission to investigate and Subpoena the Provincial Head of the Housing Department, the chief finance officer at the time, the head of supply chain in the department and the then MEC of Human Settlements. He also calls on the commission to investigate Magashule and his PA’s and the head of treasury and to ask the Auditor General in the Free State for assistance.”

“ the Commission and the people of SA …deserve to know the truth about this asbestos audit heist. I have a reasonable belief that the Free State government under Mr Magashule, was the only fertile ground in the country for this asbestos audit heist to be staged and executed. “

But his testimony was not limited only to the asbestos Audit. The evidence leaders took him through what he calls the housing Heist, operation Hlasela, the Free State Development Corporation, forgeries of his signature etc.

In the Free State Dukwana has become a bit of a local hero. Ordinary South Africans who recognize his blonde hair and his big gentle gait coming up to him and saying thank you.
Petrol attendants, white old oomies, security guards.

Even as we had coffee an Afrikaans man came to the table.
“ I hope you don’t mind” he said addressing Dukwana, “ I want to say thank you to you and if you ever need a place to hide my place is open to you.”

Dukwana laments the state of the Free State and blames the patronage system largely on Ace Magashule. A man he admits, he once protected and promoted. These two men have a long history that began in the ANC PEC in the Free State in the early 90’s. Then they served in government together both as MEC’s in various departments. In 2012 Dukwana who was MEC for economic development , was fired by Magashule. He believes it was because he refused to sign a letter given to him by the Gupta’s which would have opened the way for them to benefit from a R2 billion- rand new city project.

Dukwana told the commission how he defended Magashule, even when Lekota fired him for corruption. Now he says he has learnt his lesson and will not look away.

“ I will not make the same mistake as I did before where I will protect people when I know that they are doing wrong, so it is with that in mind that I come to this commission….We have failed the people of the Free State when we did not act on time

After his first testimony in April at the commission, Magashule threatened publicly to sue. Dukwana says he asked his legal team to get in touch with Magashule to make it easier for them. He says nothing so far has been forthcoming.

He also sounds a warning to current president Cyril Ramaphosa
“Ace is dangerous, the president needs to be strong. He is a master of deception.”

Script:


Commentary One
Mxolisi Dukwana is an activist and a former teacher. Once the ANC treasurer in the Free State, he also served as MEC in various departments of that provincial Government

Up sound hits the golf ball

But since 2012 he has had to find ways to fill his time, because that is when he challenged
ACE Magashule for the leadership of the ANC there, and soon after he was fired from the provincial government

Devi
why did he fire you?
Mxolisi
Ace doesn’t like to be challenged

Commentary Two
He says Magashule told him he was fired because the Free State cabinet needed more women. Dukwana didn’t buy it.
DEVI
Have you been able to find work since?
Mxolisi
not in the Free State I won’t be able to find work in the Free State
Devi
what does that say?
Mxolisi
one business person just greeting me, three weeks later he came to me to say hey man, I am being victimized I am not getting my money. So you have that kind of a situation where people are seen with somebody else. Ace has ears all over.

Commentary three
Ace Magashule was premier of the Free State for nine years, now he is Secretary General of the ANC. He is considered by some to have captured the Free State

Mxolisi Dukwana
He is a very ambitious person and he thinks he might become president one day, and I shudder to think what will happen if we have a president like him

LINK
Now he has become a bit of a household name in the Free State, because he is one of the few who was close to power there, who under oath at the State Capture commission, exposed the rot in the province

Up sound Zondo
Mr. Magashule was simply a blesser to many


Devi
What made you go to the Zondo commission, from where I am sitting its quite risky
Mxolisi Dukwana
I was not prepared to keep quiet because I might die. I have kids, these kids need to grow in an environment that is not toxic.We have had toxic leadership in the Free State for a long time and at the helm of that toxic leadership is Ace Magashule

Commentary Four
Former comrades, Dukwana now accuses Magashule of turning the Free State into a patronage network built on a culture of fear -and that hasn’t changed he says, just because he is now at Luthuli House

Mxolisi
In provincial government you have two parallel systems running and the one that is making decisions is the one that Ace presides over, even now while he is at Luthuli

Commentary Five
Professor Mcebisi Ndletyana has followed his testimony closely

Mcebisi Ndletyana
The cool thing about Dukwana’s testimony is that there is evidence! He is not guessing, he is not telling stories he is giving us emails. And his bravery – I don’t think we must underestimate his courage
Devi
People disappear there, people get assassinated
Mxolisi
And that is the terrible thing with corruption, and for them not to prison they go for witnesses so with corruption comes death!

Commentary Six
Dukwana first appeared at the Commission in April where he detailed how the Gupta’s bribed the former Premier

Mxolisi Dukwana April 2019
I drive to Ace Magashule’s place and I give him his million

Commentary Seven
In August he was back on the stand. He named names and gave extensive detail of two corrupt housing projects, and placed Ace Magashule at the centre of both of them.

Mxolisi
I believe these two projects will unveil the mystery behind the man. Ultimately, he will face the music



LINK Asbestos
It was supposed to be an audit to establish how many homes in the Free State had asbestos roofs but Dukwana calls it the Asbestos heist – and he has provided the commission with an email trail that leads right up into the former Premier’s office

Commentary eight
The brazenness is best understood here on these dusty streets where some homes still have harmful asbestos roofs. R255 million spent just to count them back in 2014

Mxolisi
you’re doing this for the poor. Its 2019, these people are still staying in the same houses, R255 million is gone
Devi
So where is the emergency?
Mxolisi Dukwana
It was an emergency to steal. It was not an emergency to help people

Commentary nine
Igo Mpambani and his business partner were awarded the contract in December 2014.
Even before they signed, FS province gave them an advance payment of the first R55 million

Mxolisi
Can you imagine you prepare a five-page document, you get approval, you do the job for two months and then you get R255 million, this is nice, it only happens in a province like ours

Commentary ten (pronounced Modupe)
Rathipe Molupe is a ward councilor here in Kutlwanong, and was one of the councillors asked to count the houses.
Rathipe
Yes, we did the count. I mean it’s easy you just walk past the house you don’t have to go inside the house
Devi
You can see it
Rathipe
You can see it just walking or driving past
Devi
So how long did it take do that
Rathipe
It could take 8 hours. Just one day to do the audit

Commentary eleven
At most he says it might take a week
Devi
How did you feel when you found out that that project cost R255 million?
Rathipe
I felt disgusted because the GPS coordinates are available at the office
Devi Do you think the project was worth R255 million?
Rathipe
No I think it was worth zero rands or zero millions, so it just went down the drain.

GUNSHOTS! UP SOUND

Commentary twelve
And the man who could reveal what really happened has taken his secrets to the grave.
Igo Mpambani was assassinated in 2017. But the smoking gun may be the emails from the former Premier’s office to Igo Mpambani

Mxolisi Dukwana
Every time there is payment, payment is made to this company. Ace office would have a request and that request was then sent to Mpambani by the PA to Ace Magashule at the time when Ace was still the premier, and then Mpambani responded and paid what was requested

Commentary thirteen
It was this audit and a billion- rand housing splurge that investigative journalist Pieter- Louis Myburgh revealed in his book Gangster state a few months ago. At the time Magashule threatened legal action

Pieter Louis Myburgh
When the likes of Magashule are implicated in corruption expose’s they are always very quick to threaten defamation law suits, and now almost half a year on that hasn’t happened.

Commentary Fourteen
We sent a list of allegations to Ace Magashule. His PA said they would respond but to date they have not come back to Carte Blanche.

Devi
Did he ever respond to your allegations?
Mxolisi
He will deny. He will always deny. Let him take us to court. You know under oath in court he has a lot to answer

Commentary Fifteen
And how would Magashule explain the billion rand given to the Free State by treasury, to build houses nine years ago

DEVI Link
But by December of that year they had not spent it- so they stood the risk of it going back to the fiscus. No problem for the then MEC Mosebenze Zwane who managed to move heaven and no earth to get rid of the money.


Mxolisi
What came to light is that they paid people in advance, huge sums of money
Devi
Isn’t it risky?
It’s illegal!

Commentary sixteen
Zwane now an MP, has not yet answered why he shifted a billion rand in four weeks, in a scheme the SIU later found was fraudulent with no value received. Zwane did not respond to our allegations.

Devi
But this happened in 2010?
Mxolisi
Yes/ the question that begs now is what happened to the MEC? He knew! What happened to the premier he knew! Nothing!

Commentary Seventeen
Instead Magashule has been consolidating power at Luthuli House

Mcebisi Ndletyana
So the president has to assert his grip on Luthuli House and its worrisome that quite a number of people at Luthuli house who supported CR have left for parliament and so I think ACE fully has his grip over Luthuli House

Commentary eighteen
Dukwana is concerned about the power battle between President Ramaphosa and Ace Magashule

Dukwana
He is good at scheming and pretends he doesn’t know anything, so he can’t change now

Devi Question
If we had to look at this battle between ACE and Cyril
Mcebisi Ndletyana
It’s a stale mate and I think what Cyril Ramaphosa is hoping for is for the law enforcement to act and to act fast

Pieter-Louis Myburgh
And it’s now time that they take up these issues and show the public even someone as senior as Ace Magashule politically, gets prosecuted without fear or favour

Commentary nineteen
Meanwhile Free state Municipalities are collapsing, and the Auditor General singled out the Free state for a lack of accountability and commitment towards clean administration.
Dukwana has called on Pres Ramaphosa to place the province under administration.

Mcebisi Ndletyana
Cyril Ramaphosa knows that for his presidency to gain credibility and be re- elected he has to deliver on the Zondo Commission and fortunately we are all watching this thing we know who got how much so we already know there is evidence so If Cyril doesn’t act on that evidence then he is toast he is gone.

THE END 10 05


PROMO ONE
Revelations at the Zondo commission, but still no prosecutions.
Mcebisi
And fortunately we are all watching this thing, we know who got how much! So if Cyril doesn’t act on his evidence then he is toast, he is gone!

PROMO TWO 11 seconds
Ace Magashule and Mxolisi Dukwana served together in the Free State government. Now Dukwana has told the Zondo commission the former premier is at the heart state capture in the province

PROMO THREE 11 seconds
Mxolisi Dukwana recently revealed details of what he called an Asbestos audit heist to the Zondo Commission. We went onto the streets to see for ourselves how money disappeared

At the time Magashule threatened legal action Pieter Louis Myburgh When the likes of Magashule are implicated in corruption expose’s they are always very quick to threaten defamation law suits, and now almost half a year on that hasn’t happened. Commentary Fourteen We sent a list of allegations to Ace Magashule. His PA said they would respond but to date they have not come back to Carte Blanche. Devi Did he ever respond to your allegations? Mxolisi He will deny. He will always deny. Let him take us to court. You know under oath in court he has a lot to answer Commentary Fifteen And how would Magashule explain the billion rand given to the Free State by treasury, to build houses nine years ago DEVI Link But by December of that year they had not spent it- so they stood the risk of it going back to the fiscus. No problem for the then MEC Mosebenze Zwane who managed to move heaven and no earth to get rid of the money. Mxolisi What came to light is that they paid people in advance, huge sums of money Devi Isn’t it risky? It’s illegal! Commentary sixteen Zwane now an MP, has not yet answered why he shifted a billion rand in four weeks, in a scheme the SIU later found was fraudulent with no value received. Zwane did not respond to our allegations. Devi But this happened in 2010? Mxolisi Yes/ the question that begs now is what happened to the MEC? He knew! What happened to the premier he knew! Nothing! Commentary Seventeen Instead Magashule has been consolidating power at Luthuli House Mcebisi Ndletyana So the president has to assert his grip on Luthuli House and its worrisome that quite a number of people at Luthuli house who supported CR have left for parliament and so I think ACE fully has his grip over Luthuli House Commentary eighteen Dukwana is concerned about the power battle between President Ramaphosa and Ace Magashule Dukwana He is good at scheming and pretends he doesn’t know anything, so he can’t change now Devi Question If we had to look at this battle between ACE and Cyril Mcebisi Ndletyana It’s a stale mate and I think what Cyril Ramaphosa is hoping for is for the law enforcement to act and to act fast Pieter-Louis Myburgh And it’s now time that they take up these issues and show the public even someone as senior as Ace Magashule politically, gets prosecuted without fear or favour Commentary nineteen Meanwhile Free state Municipalities are collapsing, and the Auditor General singled out the Free state for a lack of accountability and commitment towards clean administration. Dukwana has called on Pres Ramaphosa to place the province under administration. Mcebisi Ndletyana Cyril Ramaphosa knows that for his presidency to gain credibility and be re- elected he has to deliver on the Zondo Commission and fortunately we are all watching this thing we know who got how much so we already know there is evidence so If Cyril doesn’t act on that evidence then he is toast he is gone. THE END 10 05 PROMO ONE Revelations at the Zondo commission, but still no prosecutions. Mcebisi And fortunately we are all watching this thing, we know who got how much! So if Cyril doesn’t act on his evidence then he is toast, he is gone! PROMO TWO 11 seconds Ace Magashule and Mxolisi Dukwana served together in the Free State government. Now Dukwana has told the Zondo commission the former premier is at the heart state capture in the province PROMO THREE 11 seconds Mxolisi Dukwana recently revealed details of what he called an Asbestos audit heist to the Zondo Commission. We went onto the streets to see for ourselves how money disappeared

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): One liner tonight on Carte Blanche A province besieged by corruption, its former premier Ace Magashule implicated by his one- time friend and colleague Mxolisi Dukwana at the Zondo Commission. Will
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Unique Selling point Candid Interview with whistleblower Mxolisi Dukwana who has taken on ACE Magashule who some describe as South Africa’s most dangerous politician 400 pages of candid testimony already in the Zondo commission but fractured, technical and not well covered as it was over shadowed by the death of Gavin Watson.
metadata.Summary: Summary Hardly a week goes by in our politics when another salvo is fired in the ongoing battle between President Cyril Ramaphosa and Secretary General Ace Magashule. Cartoonists show the president being stabbed in the back by Magashule, or having concrete poured over his boots by a smiling Secretary General. But this battle is a battle for the soul of the ANC and by implication for the country. The president seen as offering the possibility of a stable country, Magashule seen to represent the fight back campaign that will take the country down the path of Venezuela. For nearly a decade Ace Magashule has had the run of the Free State. Allegations of corruption, lies and deceit are only part of his story. His name provokes fear and although there are allegations and even a book about his exploits, nothing ever sticks to Ace Magashule. Now his one- time friend and colleague from the ANC PEC and the Free State Government, Mxolisi Dukwana, has blown the whistle under oath at the Zondo Commission. Will his testimony carry weight, will Magashule and his patronage system be held to account and can it alter the landscape of our politics? Carte Blanche goes behind the story told at the Zondo commission and finds out why with this whistleblower from Welkom put it all on the line.
metadata.Further information: FURTHER INFORMATION The Zondo commission had a tough time keeping Mxolisi Dukwana to his statement. He is like an encyclopedia of Free State corruption, and now that he has chosen to take on the former premier, a former minister and named 30 public and private beneficiaries of corruption in his testimony, he is contacted all the time by others with their own stories of corruption, those who are too fearful to come to the commission. His latest testimony in August runs to nearly 400 pages. He implicates officials, policemen, business men, pastors and even the Free State Judiciary, whom he says have wives who do business with the provincial government. Another high- ranking official known only as Mr X , but known to Carte Blanche, is also implicated in helping to provide political cover at National level for what Dukwana calls the Asbestos Heist – A R255 million-rand audit of Asbestos rooftops that wasn’t needed. “If our law enforcement agencies were well oiled Mr Magashule and all those who aided ad abetted this asbestos audit should be doing time in jail. He went on: “To date no eradication of asbestos roofs has been carried out in any township in the Free State…I invite the commission to investigate and Subpoena the Provincial Head of the Housing Department, the chief finance officer at the time, the head of supply chain in the department and the then MEC of Human Settlements. He also calls on the commission to investigate Magashule and his PA’s and the head of treasury and to ask the Auditor General in the Free State for assistance.” “ the Commission and the people of SA …deserve to know the truth about this asbestos audit heist. I have a reasonable belief that the Free State government under Mr Magashule, was the only fertile ground in the country for this asbestos audit heist to be staged and executed. “ But his testimony was not limited only to the asbestos Audit. The evidence leaders took him through what he calls the housing Heist, operation Hlasela, the Free State Development Corporation, forgeries of his signature etc. In the Free State Dukwana has become a bit of a local hero. Ordinary South Africans who recognize his blonde hair and his big gentle gait coming up to him and saying thank you. Petrol attendants, white old oomies, security guards. Even as we had coffee an Afrikaans man came to the table. “ I hope you don’t mind” he said addressing Dukwana, “ I want to say thank you to you and if you ever need a place to hide my place is open to you.” Dukwana laments the state of the Free State and blames the patronage system largely on Ace Magashule. A man he admits, he once protected and promoted. These two men have a long history that began in the ANC PEC in the Free State in the early 90’s. Then they served in government together both as MEC’s in various departments. In 2012 Dukwana who was MEC for economic development , was fired by Magashule. He believes it was because he refused to sign a letter given to him by the Gupta’s which would have opened the way for them to benefit from a R2 billion- rand new city project. Dukwana told the commission how he defended Magashule, even when Lekota fired him for corruption. Now he says he has learnt his lesson and will not look away. “ I will not make the same mistake as I did before where I will protect people when I know that they are doing wrong, so it is with that in mind that I come to this commission….We have failed the people of the Free State when we did not act on time After his first testimony in April at the commission, Magashule threatened publicly to sue. Dukwana says he asked his legal team to get in touch with Magashule to make it easier for them. He says nothing so far has been forthcoming. He also sounds a warning to current president Cyril Ramaphosa “Ace is dangerous, the president needs to be strong. He is a master of deception.”
